## 2. Technical functionality and algorithms

**Data and cohort.** The released file ({records} records) is read only after its SHA 256 matches the frozen value. Pure parsers turn text cells into typed values: blood pressure through a regular expression, sentinel tokens such as "not_checked" into missing values, and unambiguous numeric slips repaired. Values outside the physiological ranges of `StudySpec` become missing. `CohortBuilder` applies one named method per eligibility step and records the reason for every excluded record, giving the eligible cohort of {eligible} and the analysis cohort of {analysis_cohort} pregnancies with {analysis_events} low birth weight births.

**Grouped stratified partitioning.** Records that share a registration profile (age, last menstrual date, height, registration weight and prior deliveries) form a group, and whole groups are assigned to folds while balancing events. The first fold is the held out partition of {holdout_n} pregnancies with {holdout_events} events, written with a checksum before any model step. Every model fit carries a `TrainingGuard` that refuses any held out record, and the held out outcomes are read only through one logged gate. The development partition holds {dev_n} pregnancies with {dev_events} events.

**Feature sets.** Set A holds registration characteristics, set B adds the visit two measurements, and set C adds the visit one value of each measurement recorded at both visits for at least {availability_percent} percent of records, a screen refitted in every training fold. Linear models receive values only; tree models also receive the change between visits. Sets are subclasses of one abstract `FeatureSet`.

**Models and validation.** {families} model families and a constant prevalence baseline. Pipelines impute medians with missingness indicators and scale where needed; gradient boosted trees handle missing values natively. {outer_folds} outer folds repeated {repeats} times, with hyperparameters chosen in {inner_folds} grouped inner folds by average precision, the area under the precision recall curve. Predictions are averaged per pregnancy across repeats, and paired differences between feature sets on the same pregnancies get a group bootstrap interval from {resamples} resamples. The smallest detectable difference is 2.8 bootstrap standard errors (five percent two sided test, 80 percent power).

**Prototype.** A FastAPI application with routers that validate, services that decide and a database of synthetic cases. Scoring goes only through the frozen artefact, whose checksum is verified at start; a changed file stops the server. The interface shows rank, probability with an interval, and the label "Likely" or "Not likely low birth weight" at the threshold fixed at the highest 20 percent of out of fold predictions, with how often that label is right.

## 4. Code quality practices

The package separates data access, parsing, cohort rules, partitioning, features, models, evaluation, the artefact and reporting into their own modules, and every constant lives in one frozen `StudySpec`. `FeatureSet` and `MetricStrategy` use abstraction and polymorphism. Every public class and function has a docstring and type hints; no function exceeds 50 lines and no file 300. Ruff and black run locally and in continuous integration, every output carries a checksum in `outputs/manifest.json`, and the README results are generated and tested. The history holds {commits} commits with imperative messages.

**Reading.** Adding the first visit to the second did not improve prediction of recorded low birth weight by any amount this design could detect, on development records in either model family, in any sensitivity analysis or under multiple imputation, and the single held out evaluation agrees. The second visit over registration alone shows a modest gain in discrimination. None of the {stage2_runs} prespecified Stage 2 experiments improved the model, so artefact 1.0.0 stays. On the held out records the label behaved as on development records, but overall discrimination was weaker and its ROC AUC interval includes 0.5, and the calibration slope is uncertain. With {holdout_events} held out events these intervals are wide.

**Limitations.** The predictors carry little information: fundal height is recorded only as normal or abnormal, the history counts are internally inconsistent, for example prior deliveries at or above the number of pregnancies (`docs/implementation_audit.md`), and birth weight is recorded to 0.1 kg. It is one public Tanzanian dataset (version 1 of the Zenodo record, frozen by checksum) with no facility or geographic identifier, so neither external nor geographic validation is possible, and the release contains no ethics approval or consent statement; a request was sent to the producers on 21 October 2026. The development partition holds {dev_events} events, so only differences of roughly the detectable size could be seen. The outcome is birth weight under the care actually given, and nothing here shows that acting on a prediction would change it. The prototype runs on synthetic cases only and has not been validated for any pregnancy; a larger independent cohort is needed before any claim about use in practice.
